chunks: Ḥammād narrated from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about al-mutʿah: whether it is among the four. He said, “No, and not even among seventy.”

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the one being asked for the ruling
key_terms.السَّبْعِينَ: a hyperbolic number used to emphasize that mutʿah is not included in such a count
key_terms.الْأَرْبَعِ: the legal limit of four wives referenced in the question
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةِ: temporary marriage being asked about in this legal context

ai.seo_question: Is mutʿah counted among the four wives in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that mutʿah is not counted within the limit of four wives. The Imam عليه السلام emphatically rejects including it in that number, indicating a distinct legal status for temporary marriage.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4594 - Hammad narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (as) was asked about Mutah (temporary marriage) - whether it is counted as part of the four [wives].
Imam (as) said: "No, and not even among seventy."
